newsitem.title: USA: Republicans complain about Clinton train trip.
newsitem.headline: Republicans complain about Clinton train trip.

text.p: Republican Party chairman Haley Barbour charged Monday that President Clinton's campaign is "sticking the taxpayers" for most of the costs of Clinton's whistlestop train trip to the Democratic national convention.
He said his party would file a complaint with the Federal Election Commission over the matter.

"Today the Republican National Committee will file a complaint against the Clinton-Gore campaign for its sticking the taxpayers with 90 percent of the cost of President Clinton's train trip preceeding the Democratic National Convention," he told reporters.

Barbour said the Clinton campaign has claimed "the train trip was purely transportation and should be treated as the same as a trip on Air Force One." But Barbour contended it was "a continuous campaign trip with many stops" and said the complaint will seek reimbursement for the government of the full cost of the trip to Chicago.

Details of how much it cost were not available and the Clinton campaign referred inquiries to a news conference held Aug. 29 by White House press secretary Mike McCurry, who said the campaign was picking up $113,000 of the train trip's cost.

When a questioner asked whether taxpayers would pick up $400,000 of costs, McCurry said, "The taxpayer costs I can't detail for you but they are substantial as they are when the president travels on Air Force One or anytime he travels in his capacity as president."
McCurry said Monday that questions about the financing of the train trip had been exhaustively examined. "It wasn't an issue then, it isn't an issue now," McCurry said.
Asked if the taxpayers had picked up 90 percent of the costs, McCurry replied: "Not based on what I saw."
He declined to detail how much of the tab had gone to the taxpayers, but repeated that the costs for the president's travel are "always substantial."
